No — leaf2 is not in pathtracer/ right now. The current tree is the round-2 "wide" layout: 64-byte nodes holding both children's AABBs+payloads inline, with leaves being a SINGLE triangle (the leaf payload is just the triangle index, so leaves take no node slot). This session's own run confirms it: `info: bvh nodes=69450 depth=16` for 69,451 triangles, i.e. n-1 internal nodes and zero leaf nodes, which is only possible with leaf size 1.

Why leaf2 was dropped: I did implement it in round 2 (scratch/make_leaf2.py) as a candidate — two triangles per leaf with the leaf's AABB being the union of the two. It measured slower than leaf size 1, so I reverted it with scratch/revert_leaf2.py and kept leaf-1. The reason is geometric: the bunny is a thin shell, so a leaf's box is mostly empty space; merging two triangles fattens the boxes, so rays descend deeper and pay more triangle intersections than the saved node visits return. That matches the leaf-size sweep recorded in src/bvh.cpp's comment (leaf size 1 ≈ 55.4 ms average vs leaf size 4 ≈ 64.4 ms in round 2), and it is also why this round's 4-wide experiment kept single-triangle leaves — the only reason to widen nodes is fewer dependent loads, not fewer leaf slots.

Side note from the same thread of evidence: the 4-wide node variant (scratch/w4, still leaf-1) is currently a wash against the live build (best 44.2–47.2 ms vs 44.7–49.8 ms interleaved, within noise), so it has not been adopted either; the tree-depth reduction is being paid for by extra registers/work per node.

Why leaf2 was dropped, from the measurements:
1. First leaf2 attempt measured ~33.5 ms, which looked like a big win — but that build was buggy: merged leaf bounds dropped roughly half the triangles, so the timing was meaningless. After the fix, RMSE vs the 1024-spp reference came back statistically identical to baseline (0.475902 vs 0.475898), confirming correctness but not speed.
2. Honest same-session A/B of the fixed leaf2 build vs the round-2 baseline and vs wide1: leaf2 bests 49.0/49.9/54.5 ms, R02 49.8/50.2/52.3 ms, wide1 44.3/45.7/46.4 ms. So leaf2 was a wash against the baseline and ~8% slower than wide1 — the wider leaf bounds make the bunny's thin-shell geometry leak more empty space into each leaf, and the extra triangle test per leaf costs more than the node visits saved.
3. Consequently I ran scratch/revert_leaf2.py, which restored the leaf-1 wide-node tree in pathtracer/, and that is the tree being benchmarked today (~44-46 ms best at 512x512/64spp).

Related and consistent: in the current round-3 experiment I built a 4-wide node variant (scratch/w4, tree depth 8 vs 16, 25,760 nodes) and it is also slower (~46-47 vs ~45 ms best), so the evidence points the same way — for this mesh, keeping leaves to one triangle and the fan-out at two is what wins; the extra per-level work of a wider fan-out outweighs the shorter tree. I'm logging all of this to pathtracer_writer_log.txt.
